newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Delta, Yuasa sign T$1.3B deal.
newsitem.headline: Delta, Yuasa sign T$1.3B deal.

text.p: Taiwan's Delta Electronics said on Saturday it has signed a contract with Japan's Yuasa Corp to invest a combined T$1.3 billion in a battery plant in Taiwan.

The plant, to be owned 45 percent each by Delta and Yuasa and 10 percent by company employees, would produce 10 million nickel-metal hydride batteries per month when it reaches full capacity in 1999, Delta said in a statement.
Such a capacity would make the joint venture one of the world's four largest battery producers, Delta said.
"We all know that Yuasa has a long, distinguished history in the battery industry... We are very honoured to be Yuasa's partner," Delta chairman Cheng Chung-hua said in the statement.
"We believe our venture will show strong competitiveness," Cheng added.
Nickel-metal hydride batteries are the type used in common electronic products.
A spokesman for Delta said his company plans to issue US$100 million in convertible bonds to raise funds for the plant and other operational purposes.
